question: Was claim GC-010 handled in line with policy?

report.interpretation: A compliance review of quality-review claim file GC-010. Cover and settlement rules use the incident date (2026-02-10). Procedural rules use the decision date (2026-02-20). The review ran through check_claim_compliance, and I am summarising its verdict.
report.answer: No. GC-010 is NON_COMPLIANT, with two HIGH-severity breaches that come from the same cause. The incident was on 2026-02-10, so the older motor policy version (v5.3) applies. Under it, driving on an expired licence is treated as unlicensed driving, which is an absolute exclusion with no rebuttal (POL-MTR-002 §3.4, v5.3; §3.1, v5.3). The driver's licence had been expired for 18 days, and it was renewed 9 days after the incident. The handler applied the newer v6.0 30-day rebuttal and set the exclusion aside. That override is itself a breach, because the claim had to be denied under POL-CLM-001 §7.2, v4.2. The L3 and L4 approvers had no authority to override an absolute exclusion, so the acceptance and the 5,800 payment are void and must be re-made (POL-AUT-003 §4.3, v3.1; §1.2, v3.1; POL-CLM-001 §7.1, v4.2). The other eight areas passed: cover, notification, triage, assessment, fraud, documentation, service levels and settlement. The settlement arithmetic was correct (6,600 gross less 800 excess gives 5,800), but the payment should not have been made at all. The recorded verdict in compliance_results also says NON_COMPLIANT, but it shows 1 breach. The live review found 2 (exclusions and authority).

Claim must be notified within 30 calendar days of the incident

Unlicensed driving is an ABSOLUTE exclusion in v5.3, which applies to incidents before 2026-03-01. An expired licence is treated as no licence and no rebuttal is available. An override of an absolute exclusion is itself a breach.
Claim must be triaged within 1 business day and assigned the correct track
An assessment is required on a standard claim, and a desktop assessment is permitted at handler discretion
An absolute exclusion may not be overridden at any level, and a decision outside delegated authority is void
Every claim must be scored and referred if the score is 60 or above
Required decision-stage and settlement-stage documents must be on file
Acknowledgement, triage, decision, communication, payment and status-update timeframes
Settlement is the assessed amount less basic excess, with no additional excess, ITC or waiver
